title: Carry
source: Lecture9_MGT595_2023.pdf (beamer, full text extracted in-context; two papers)
papers: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen (2008), 'Carry Trades and Currency Crashes', NBER Macro Annual

page_groups.content: Carry trade example (Nov 8 2007): BORROW at 0.87% 3m JPY LIBOR (funding currency), INVEST at 7.09% 3m AUD LIBOR (investment currency), HOPE JPY doesn't appreciate. UIP violation = 'forward premium puzzle'. Large FX moves WITHOUT news (Oct 7-8 1998 yen). 'Up by the stairs and down by the elevator.' Literature: near-random-walk FX (Meese-Rogoff), funding liquidity (BP 2007), transaction costs, rare disasters (Farhi-Gabaix), consumption risk (Lustig-Verdelhan).

Data 1986-2006: 8 currencies vs USD (AUD CAD JPY NZD NOK CHF GBP EUR); z_t = (i*-i) - delta_s = carry-trade excess return; UIP: E[z]=0. CFTC futures positions of non-commercial traders (speculators); JPM risk reversals 1998-2006 (price of crash insurance). SUMMARY STATS (REAL Table 1): interest differential i*-i: AUD .006, NZD .009, NOK .005, GBP .005, CAD .002, EUR -.001, CHF -.004, JPY -.007. Mean z: NZD .013, AUD .009, GBP .009, NOK .007, CAD .004, EUR .003, CHF -.001, JPY -.004. SKEWNESS: AUD -0.322, NZD -0.297, CAD -0.143, GBP -0.094, NOK -0.019, EUR +0.131, CHF +0.144, JPY +0.318. RISK REVERSALS: JPY +1.059, CHF +0.409, NOK +0.350, EUR +0.329, GBP +0.009, CAD -0.099, AUD -0.426, NZD -0.467. Graphically: skewness and risk reversals DECLINE in i*-i (scatter with fitted line); speculator futures positions INCREASE in i*-i (JPY -0.097, CHF -0.067, EUR +0.031, CAD +0.059, GBP +0.052).

PREDICTIVE PANEL REGRESSIONS (REAL Table 2, quarterly, country FE, coefficients on i*-i with SEs): predicting z(t+tau): t+1: 2.17 (0.78); t+2: 2.24; t+3: 1.87; t+4: 1.50; t+5: 1.11; t+6: 0.76; t+10: -0.04 - positive carry predicts positive returns (UIP violation) fading over ~2 years. Predicting FUTURES positions: t+1: 8.26 (5.06) up to t+6 4.72, fading. Predicting SKEWNESS: t+1: -23.92 (3.87); stays -23 to -21 through t+7, -12.9 at t+9: carry predicts persistent NEGATIVE skewness = crash risk. VAR(3) impulse responses confirm: shock to i*-i raises cumulated excess return above UIP line, raises futures positions, pushes skewness negative. Kernel densities: high-carry (blue, i*-i>.005) distribution right-shifted with fat LEFT tail; low-carry (red) mirror image.

PRICE OF CRASH RISK (REAL Table 3, 1998-2006): Skewness(t+1) on i*-i: -28.51 (11.59); on z_t: -3.34 (0.60) - after LOSSES, future skewness is HIGHER (crash risk lower); on Futures: -0.26. RiskRev_t on z_t: +7.87 (1.39) - after losses the PRICE of insurance RISES even though risk fell ('price of insurance goes up after an earthquake although the risk of another is low') - slow-moving capital. R2 up to 0.41. UNWINDING (REAL Table 4, weekly): dVIX x sign(i*-i): dFutures -1.47 (0.77), dFutures(t+1) -1.29, dRiskRev -5.33, z_t -0.43 (0.11) - VIX spikes coincide with carry losses, position unwinds, and pricier insurance. TED versions similar (dTED: z(t+1) -0.57). Funding liquidity dries up -> carry unwinds.

CO-MOVEMENT (REAL Table 5): pairwise FX correlation regressed on |i1-i2|: -10.89 (3.81); -16.39 with time FE; -13.41 with pair FE - currencies with SIMILAR interest rates co-move (funding currencies together, investment currencies together): carry trades create a common factor. UIP-violation interaction (Table 6): return predictability from carry is concentrated after high-VIX states. CONCLUSION: speculators partly correct UIP but face crash risk from their own funding constraints; crash risk rises with carry, past gains, and positions; insurance price rises with carry and after losses; VIX spikes = losses + unwind; limits to arbitrage sustain the forward premium puzzle.

GENERALIZED CARRY: 'the return you earn if market conditions stay constant.' return = carry + E(price appreciation) + unexpected shock. Directly observable ex ante. Questions: does generalized UIP/EH hold anywhere? Futures definition: fully-collateralized excess return r(t+1) = (S(t+1)-F)/F; carry C = (S-F)/F if S(t+1)=S. Applied per class: CURRENCIES: C proportional to (rf* - rf) - the interest differential, as usual. EQUITIES: F = S(1+rf) - E(D) so C = E(D)/S - rf = expected dividend yield minus local risk-free; Gordon: E(R) - rf = D/S - rf + g links carry to expected returns. COMMODITIES: F = S(1+rf-delta) so C = delta - rf = convenience yield minus rf. FIXED INCOME: C = (yT - rf) [slope] - D_mod x (y(T-1) - yT) [roll down]; slope trades = difference of two carries. TREASURIES/CREDIT: duration-adjusted C/D. OPTIONS: carry = -theta/F + vega x vol-rolldown/F.

Data: 13 equity index futures countries, 20 currencies, 24 commodities, 10 country bond markets, 6 US Treasury maturity portfolios (from 1971), 8 credit portfolios (1973), index options two delta groups (1996), 20+ years everywhere. Portfolio construction: rank-weighted long-short w = z(rank(C) - (N+1)/2), a dollar long and short; current carry and carry1-12 (seasonal-adjusted) versions.

GLOBAL CARRY RETURNS (REAL Table): per class, Carry vs EW-long: Global equities 9.14/10.42 SR 0.88 vs EW SR 0.32; FI 10Y 3.85/7.45 SR 0.52 vs 0.74; FI 10Y-2Y slope SR 0.66; US Treasuries SR 0.68; Commodities 11.22/18.78 SR 0.60 vs 0.08; Currencies 5.29/7.80 SR 0.68 vs 0.36; Credit SR 0.47; Options calls SR 0.37 (EW -0.23); Options puts 179/99 SR 1.80 (EW -1.01). ALL ASSET CLASSES (GLOBAL CARRY FACTOR): mean 6.75, stdev 6.12, skewness -0.02, kurtosis 5.24, SHARPE 1.10 vs EW 0.47. Skewness -0.02 at the diversified level: LIMITED crash risk globally (unlike currency carry alone -0.68). Cumulative GCF plot: strong, steady, dwarfs currency carry.

STATIC vs DYNAMIC decomposition (REAL): E[carry return] = passive (average weights x average returns) + dynamic (timing). % dynamic by class: Equities 101%, FI 10Y 86%, FI slope 99%, US Treasuries 42%, Commodities 64%, Currencies 58%, Credit 30%, Calls 111%, Puts 100% - carry is mostly a DYNAMIC signal, not a static tilt (except Treasuries/credit). Correlations of carry strategies ACROSS classes are LOW (max FX-credit 0.31; most 0-0.17) - diversification is the engine of the 1.10 Sharpe. Carry is DIFFERENT from value and momentum: regressions on passive-long, value, momentum, TSMOM leave alphas: GCF alpha 0.53 (t 6.52) unconditional, 0.44 (t 5.51) with all controls, IR 1.05-1.24; per class alphas mostly significant (equities 0.77 t 4.51; FX 0.30 t 2.31; puts 12.55 t 4.55).

RISK EXPOSURES (REAL): liquidity shocks: Currencies +0.88 (t 3.62), Credit +1.24 (t 3.78), Puts +0.57 (t 2.48), Commodities +0.26 (t 2.36); volatility changes: Currencies -1.03 (t -6.46), Commodities -0.42 (t -2.74), FI 10Y -0.54 (t -2.25), Credit -0.58, Puts -0.62; Treasuries OPPOSITE (+0.54 vol). Carry EXPANSIONS vs DRAWDOWNS (REAL, annualized mean): Equities 15.03 vs -6.15; FI 10Y 10.84 vs -13.90; Commodities 21.49 vs -13.23; Currencies 10.06 vs -6.81; Credit 0.60 vs -0.50; Puts 258 vs -22. Three GCF drawdowns: Aug1972-Sep1975 (-19.6%), Mar1980-Jun1982 (-26.8%), Aug2008-Feb2009 (-7.2%) - ALL span recessions: carry premium looks like compensation for recession/liquidity/volatility risk. TIMING strategies (long/short vs zero carry): SR equities 0.40, FI 0.65-0.72, currencies 0.78, credit 0.64, puts 1.01. Conclusion: carry predicts returns in EVERY class; broad rejection of UIP/EH; E(R) varies over time and across assets; drivers = recession, liquidity, volatility risk; not a pure crash story at the global level.

gap_analysis: All BNP and KMP numbers above are taken verbatim from the in-context PDF text (tables extracted cleanly); no image-only tables were needed.
BNP TED-spread chart is described as stylized in the app (the deck's own TED figure is an image); the VIX/TED regression coefficients used are the real Table 4 values.
KMP 'coefficient <> 1 depending on asset class' regression detail (their Table 3) is not in the deck text beyond the summary line; the app states the qualitative finding only.
Options carry magnitudes (means 64/179 etc.) are in %/month units per the deck table; the app displays Sharpe ratios and flags units where shown.
